complaint.name: Synthetic Customer 039
complaint.title: [DEMO C039] A Sheets action is missing after catalog discovery
complaint.description: The agent is missing a required Sheets action after catalog discovery, despite it appearing in the current catalog; a provider outage may be involved.

hypotheses.description: Probable cause: cedar’s missing Sheets action was due to tool discovery truncation/incomplete pagination on the incident-time googlesheets catalog path. The canonical production log shows discovery returned only 20 tools with more pages available, and the needed action was on a later page even though that catalog version contained it. A controlled synthetic comparison reproduced the first-page truncation pattern under the original condition and found the tool after the corrected condition completed pagination.
assumptions: This diagnosis is scoped to the observed cedar discovery failure path and does not prove the mechanism for every blocked business operation in the window.

The controlled reproduce records are synthetic/provider-mock observations that discriminate the pagination/config variable, not direct proof of every production follow-on request after the first page.
The supplied production logs do not show whether cedar later attempted pagination and then filtered or dropped the tool.

hypotheses.description: Alternative: a tenant-specific configuration or toolkit/version behavior changed discovery outcome for cedar, but the supplied evidence does not identify the exact production config or pin difference. This could explain why cedar remained on the first page while maple did not show impact, but it is secondary to the direct observation that cedar’s incident-time discovery was truncated.
assumptions: The controlled comparison changed sheets_configuration, but the incident record set does not include canonical cedar/maple config history or toolkit pin history.
The unrelated deployment record is not evidence of a tool-executor change.
An empty time-bounded dependency result is a telemetry gap, not proof that no relevant config changed.

hypotheses.description: Broad provider outage is unlikely for the observed failed execution. The request succeeded with HTTP 200, provider reachability was reported true, and a same-window comparison tenant succeeded against the same provider. A narrow provider-side anomaly cannot be fully excluded from the supplied evidence, but it is not needed to explain the observed failure mechanism.
assumptions: The synthetic controlled comparison mainly shows the issue can occur without a live provider outage.
No provider-side per-request traces are supplied, so a very narrow provider anomaly is not conclusively excluded.

recommended_actions: tool_discovery_truncation_remediation: paginate discovery or raise the googlesheets discovery limit, then use the exact returned action slug from the intended version. This is a proposed next step and has not been executed here.

collect_missing_telemetry: capture canonical cedar discovery telemetry for page tokens plus any follow-on pagination requests/responses so future incidents can distinguish never-paginated from paginated-then-filtered/dropped.
align_telemetry_windows: align blocked-operation metrics with discovery-stage telemetry so tenant impact can be tied more precisely to first-page truncation versus a later execution-stage drop.

update_and_test_toolkit_pin: compare effective googlesheets discovery configuration/toolkit behavior for cedar versus maple and collect canonical config or pin-history records for the incident window.
monitor_provider: do not prioritize a broad provider-outage explanation unless new provider-error evidence appears; continue monitoring because provider failure is not fully impossible.
limitations: The supplied canonical logs do not include the full discovery response body, action list, page token, or subsequent cedar pagination requests/responses for 09:50–10:15.
No canonical incident-time config-history or toolkit-pin record is provided for cedar or maple, so the reason cedar stopped at first-page results is unverified.
The reproduce tool provides precomputed synthetic/provider-mock observations and does not execute a live production experiment.
Observed tenant impact metrics are correlated with the discovery problem, but the evidence does not prove that all 380 blocked operations were caused by this exact mechanism.

findings.statement: At 10:05, cedar's googlesheets discovery returned status 200 with list_limit=20, returned_tools=20, has_more=true, and the requested tool marked as being on a later page while the catalog version still contained it.
In the controlled synthetic sandbox, the original condition reproduced the same first-page truncation pattern, while the corrected condition completed pagination and found the requested Sheets tool.

Impact was concentrated in cedar: 602 requests, 0 transport failures, but 380 business operations blocked, queue_depth 108, and p95 latency 1440 ms; comparison tenant maple had 516 requests, 0 blocked operations, queue_depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.
A same-window comparison tenant separates this from a broad provider outage: maple had status 200, same provider available, and an unrelated Sheets read succeeding.
No relevant tool-executor deployment is evidenced in the supplied window; the only recorded deployment was an unrelated support-dashboard release.

The observed cedar discovery path returned 200 and showed the needed action existed in the catalog version but on a later page, so the visible failure mechanism appears before any provider-outage explanation is needed for this request.

followups.question: What canonical discovery and executor records exist for incident window 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–10:15:00Z with null/empty filters first, then narrowed by service=tool-executor and any Sheets-related literal substrings, to show: the discovery request, returned tool/action count, whether the missing Sheets action slug was present or truncated, request latency/error rate, backlog, and the affected tenant(s) versus comparison tenants?

Were there any timed changes or dependencies overlapping the window—catalog/discovery service changes, toolkit/version pin changes, auth/connection changes for Sheets, feature-flag/config updates, or upstream Google/provider status signals—and is there canonical evidence tying any change to the affected tenant/request rather than only temporal proximity?

Among the leading hypotheses—tool discovery truncation, connection surface/isolation or auth mismatch, provider failure, and internal regression—which best matches the observed failed discovery/execution path for the affected tenant, and what discriminating control or comparison (same tenant different action, different tenant same action, pre/post window, or current catalog vs returned discovery payload) can confirm or contradict each mechanism?
Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.

notes: Current incident context contains no canonical evidence records; no diagnosis is justified yet.
Start with broad/null-filter log and metric queries because exact-match filters can silently miss records with absent timestamps/service fields.

Use canonical source records for discovery responses, executor logs, queue/backlog metrics, and auth/connection events; do not rely on derived connection/refresh convenience views as independent proof.

Scope the tenant impact explicitly: identify affected tenant/request IDs, compare failure rate and latency to at least one unaffected tenant if available, and note whether impact is isolated or widespread.

If the action appears in the current catalog but not in the returned discovery payload during the incident, treat that as a hypothesis for truncation or version/pin mismatch, not proof until the exact returned payload is observed.
Provider outage remains only a hypothesis unless requests demonstrably reached the provider and failed there; if the action is missing before execution, prioritize pre-provider mechanisms.
Look for counter-evidence: successful Sheets discovery/execution in the same window, healthy non-Sheets discovery, or a comparison tenant receiving the supposedly missing action.

Material missing verification: canonical discovery payloads for the affected request, tenant-scoped impact metrics, and any overlapping catalog/version/auth changes. Optional reassurance later: code-level inspection or broader historical similarity review.

payload.question: What canonical discovery and executor records exist for incident window 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–10:15:00Z with null/empty filters first, then narrowed by service=tool-executor and any Sheets-related literal substrings, to show: the discovery request, returned tool/action count, whether the missing Sheets action slug was present or truncated, request latency/error rate, backlog, and the affected tenant(s) versus comparison tenants?

notes: No canonical timed change is shown for the affected service in the incident window: the tool-executor deployment query for 09:50–10:15 returns no records (ev_abed50f2fc18), while the only observed deployment is an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05Z with no tenant/request tie to cedar req-39 (ev_4103779983c7, sheets-discovery-039:deployments:0).

Observed request behavior points away from a Google/provider outage as the primary overlap: cedar req-39 received a 200 discovery response where the requested Sheets tool existed in the version but was on a later page beyond list_limit=20; maple simultaneously shows the same provider available and an unrelated read succeeding; dependency telemetry also says provider_api_reachable=true (ev_1b8d7225c1b0, sheets-discovery-039:logs:0; ev_1b8d7225c1b0, sheets-discovery-039:logs:1; ev_63cc0806cce6, sheets-discovery-039:dependencies:0).

Tenant impact is isolated to cedar in the supplied metrics rather than platform-wide: cedar shows 602 requests, 0 failures, 380 business operations blocked, queue_depth 108, p95 latency 1440 ms, while maple shows 516 requests, 0 blocked, queue_depth 0, p95 160 ms (ev_fa5228b7ff1d, sheets-discovery-039:metrics:0; ev_fa5228b7ff1d, sheets-discovery-039:metrics:1). This is impact evidence, not evidence of a timed dependency change.

Important gaps: there is no canonical evidence here of catalog/discovery service changes, toolkit/version pin changes, Sheets auth/connection changes, or feature-flag/config updates tied to cedar req-39. The sandbox controlled comparison suggests configuration can discriminate outcome, but it is precomputed reproduction evidence and not a canonical production change record for the affected tenant/request (ev_154da898e8ad, sheets-discovery-039:reproduce:0; ev_154da898e8ad, sheets-discovery-039:reproduce:1).

Null-filter canonical records already include the key discovery/executor observation at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z for tenant cedar: tool-executor request req-39 returned HTTP 200 for toolkit googlesheets with list_limit=20, returned_tools=20, has_more=true, and the requested Sheets tool was on a later page while the version still contained it, consistent with omission from the first page rather than disappearance from the catalog (ev_1b8d7225c1b0 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:0).

The narrowed service=tool-executor, time-window, literal "sheets" query reproduced the same two canonical log records: affected cedar discovery above, plus comparison tenant maple with HTTP 200 and same_provider_available=true / unrelated_read_succeeds=true, which is counter-evidence to a broad provider outage in this window (ev_382ef84125f4 / sheets-discovery-039:logs:0, sheets-discovery-039:logs:1).

Canonical metrics at the same timestamp show tenant-scoped impact concentrated in cedar despite zero request failures: cedar had 602 requests, 0 failures, 380 business_operations_blocked, queue_depth 108, p95 latency 1440 ms, versus maple with 516 requests, 0 failures, 0 blocked ops, queue_depth 0, p95 160 ms (ev_fa5228b7ff1d / sheets-discovery-039:metrics:0, sheets-discovery-039:metrics:1; also returned by narrowed query ev_9b46018c5c9d).

Gaps/limits: no canonical record here gives the exact missing action slug string, only that the requested tool was on a later page and present in the version; no tool-executor deployments were recorded in-window, and dependency metadata only shows provider_api_reachable=true, which does not by itself prove or disprove the specific discovery failure path (ev_abed50f2fc18; ev_63cc0806cce6 / sheets-discovery-039:dependencies:0).

hypotheses.description: Broad provider outage is unlikely for the observed failed execution. The request succeeded with HTTP 200, provider reachability was reported true, and a same-window comparison tenant succeeded against the same provider. A narrow provider-side anomaly cannot be fully excluded from the supplied evidence, but it is not needed to explain the observed failure mechanism.
assumptions: The synthetic controlled comparison mainly shows the issue can occur without a live provider outage.
No provider-side per-request traces are supplied, so a very narrow provider anomaly is not conclusively excluded.

recommended_actions: tool_discovery_truncation_remediation: paginate discovery or raise the googlesheets discovery limit, then use the exact returned action slug from the intended version. This is a proposed next step and has not been executed here.

collect_missing_telemetry: capture canonical cedar discovery telemetry for page tokens plus any follow-on pagination requests/responses so future incidents can distinguish never-paginated from paginated-then-filtered/dropped.
align_telemetry_windows: align blocked-operation metrics with discovery-stage telemetry so tenant impact can be tied more precisely to first-page truncation versus a later execution-stage drop.

update_and_test_toolkit_pin: compare effective googlesheets discovery configuration/toolkit behavior for cedar versus maple and collect canonical config or pin-history records for the incident window.
monitor_provider: do not prioritize a broad provider-outage explanation unless new provider-error evidence appears; continue monitoring because provider failure is not fully impossible.
limitations: The supplied canonical logs do not include the full discovery response body, action list, page token, or subsequent cedar pagination requests/responses for 09:50–10:15.
No canonical incident-time config-history or toolkit-pin record is provided for cedar or maple, so the reason cedar stopped at first-page results is unverified.
The reproduce tool provides precomputed synthetic/provider-mock observations and does not execute a live production experiment.
Observed tenant impact metrics are correlated with the discovery problem, but the evidence does not prove that all 380 blocked operations were caused by this exact mechanism.

findings.statement: At 10:05, cedar's googlesheets discovery returned status 200 with list_limit=20, returned_tools=20, has_more=true, and the requested tool marked as being on a later page while the catalog version still contained it.
In the controlled synthetic sandbox, the original condition reproduced the same first-page truncation pattern, while the corrected condition completed pagination and found the requested Sheets tool.

Impact was concentrated in cedar: 602 requests, 0 transport failures, but 380 business operations blocked, queue_depth 108, and p95 latency 1440 ms; comparison tenant maple had 516 requests, 0 blocked operations, queue_depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.
A same-window comparison tenant separates this from a broad provider outage: maple had status 200, same provider available, and an unrelated Sheets read succeeding.
No relevant tool-executor deployment is evidenced in the supplied window; the only recorded deployment was an unrelated support-dashboard release.

The observed cedar discovery path returned 200 and showed the needed action existed in the catalog version but on a later page, so the visible failure mechanism appears before any provider-outage explanation is needed for this request.
